children.objective: Focus on CTA-level source tiling while each output thread traverses source tiles serially, distinguishing this from T3’s warp-parallel source reduction. Stage only x, y, z and mass for force calculations; treat full-record staging, including unused velocities, as a separate measured variant if explored. Use safe block-wide synchronization for partial source tiles and a grid-stride output mapping so coverage does not depend on items_per_block being available to device code. Keep shared-memory use within the configured limit, and check correctness before timing.
children.subject: CTA shared-memory tiling of force-relevant source fields

children.objective: Use controlled arithmetic ablations in the one-thread-per-target loop: compare the unchanged expression, an rsqrtf-based reciprocal-distance variant without target-mass cancellation, a target-mass-cancelled variant retaining the original sqrt/division path, and then their combination. Keep other transformations separate so the effect of each can be judged. Do not enable global fast math. Validate tolerance, finite outputs, and exact mass preservation on all required cases before comparing repeated timings.
children.subject: Isolated ablations of reciprocal-square-root arithmetic and target-mass cancellation

children.objective: Test warp-level lane-parallel source accumulation and force reduction without a CTA shared-memory source tile, keeping this distinct from T1. Handle arbitrary N, source tails, and self interaction; document the effect of strided AoS source loads and changed reduction order. Validate numerical tolerance, finite outputs, and exact mass preservation across the required cases before repeated timing.
children.subject: Warp-parallel source reduction without block-wide source tiling

children.objective: With the baseline-style source loop and without shared-memory tiling or warp reductions, investigate launch geometry and output work granularity. Tune block and items_per_block within the stated ranges, using a correct grid-stride mapping so every particle is written for all supported configurations and sizes. Compare repeated official timings and correctness; report the selected configuration and evidence rather than assuming larger blocks or more work per block are faster.
children.subject: Launch geometry and grid-stride work granularity
